answer: Sybil resistance arises when trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph: a sybil cluster separated by a sparse external cut has low conductance, so few walk trajectories enter or leave it. Mixing and min-cut transitivity bounds therefore cap its stationary mass and aggregate voting weight, even if the cluster amplifies internal endorsements. The reef, ripple, and atlas of attestations remain locally dense but globally constrained.
